Subject: Kickoff: sequencing for MSA/DPA/order-form and evidence windows

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Our leadership wants a clear gated plan so we can hit a firm signature date and line up our implementation resources. High-level asks:
- Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) that maps MSA -> DPA -> order form sequencing and the minimum evidence we need at each gate?
- Our legal team expects the MSA to land before they start detailed DPA review, but procurement won't commit to the order form until the DPA is approved. Is that sequencing typical for Redwood?
- Target milestones: internal sign-off by 10/01 for a pilot order, production gating by 11/01. Can you confirm feasibility and key owners?

If possible, send a draft MAP and a short list of the SOC/SSO or other artifacts legal will need in the DPA review.

Appreciate it — Anna

anna.lewis@clearstreamhealth.com

Subject: Re: Kickoff: sequencing for MSA/DPA/order-form and evidence windows

Hi Anna — great to connect and thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: yes, we commonly sequence MSA -> DPA -> order form for customers with regulated data, and we can support a timeboxed evidence window for the DPA review. I attached a draft MAP that breaks out milestones, owners, and required artifacts at each gate. Two quick notes up front:
1) To unblock a pilot quickly we can propose a limited-scope MSA (standard commercial terms + data isolation clause) and run the pilot under strict tenant isolation until the DPA is finalized.
2) SOC2 + SAML SSO configuration and a redacted architecture diagram are the three items legal usually wants first; we'll capture specifics in the MAP.

Please see attached: ClearStream_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP w/ suggested dates + owners).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: help scope the pilot MSA clause set and proposed acceptance criteria (can you own?)
- Laura: will you pre-review the MSA redline so we can hand over to ClearStream legal the same day?
- Anna: can you confirm the primary procurement contact for contract execution and your legal reviewer?

I can turn this into a short mutual action plan email that maps to your 10/01 pilot target.

Cheers,
Evelyn
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — the MAP is helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal side:
- Legal has confirmed they prefer an MSA first, then DPA; procurement will not sign the order form until the DPA is in place. That's non-negotiable for our compliance posture.
- For the DPA review legal will expect: SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC report in process + remediation plan), SAML SSO details (IdP metadata), data flow diagram showing PHI/PII boundaries, and a list of sub-processors.
- Can Redwood commit to a 5-business-day response SLA for evidence requests during the DPA review window? That will determine whether we can complete DPA review inside your proposed window.

If you can send a proposed sequence that honors MSA -> DPA -> order form and includes who will provide each artifact and by when, we can confirm internally.

Best,
Anna

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ClearStream sequencing proposal and owners (draft)

Team — pulling together a tight sequencing plan for ClearStream (deal CLR-2026-0047). Anna confirmed MSA -> DPA -> order form ordering and asked for a 5-business-day evidence SLA during the DPA review. They want pilot sign 10/01; pilot acceptance gating for launch.

Proposed sequencing (high level):
1) MSA (limited-scope pilot terms) — owner: Laura (legal) — Target sent to customer 2026-09-15, comment cycle 3 business days.
2) DPA (technical/controls review) — owner: Karthik (technical lead) + Security (support) — Target evidence window 2026-09-20 through 2026-09-27. We can commit to 5-business-day turnaround for the items we own (SOC reference, SSO metadata, subprocessor list).
3) Order form (procurement) — owner: Evelyn (AM) + Jordan (revops) — order form to be issued upon DPA sign-off; DocuSign path set up by 2026-09-28.
4) Pilot acceptance (limited scope) — engineering acceptance criteria to be included in MAP; target pilot start 10/01, pilot acceptance window 10/01–10/14.

Open questions / risk items:
- If SOC2 is not current we need a mid-path: provide SOC in process + compensating controls (this may stretch DPA duration).
- Evidence request volume: if legal asks for system-level logs or endpoint details we should push back to a standard evidence checklist to avoid ad-hoc tickets.
- Pricing/term concessions: procurement may ask for a short-term discount for pilot; if so, Jordan please confirm allowable ranges.

Laura — can you draft the limited-scope MSA language focused on pilot isolation and liability caps? Karthik — please assemble the evidence packet and confirm the 5-business-day SLA is feasible. Jordan — I'll need a DocuSign template ready to go for order form issuance.

I'll convert this into an updated MAP and send back to Anna once we have Laura's draft.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Subject: Re: Kickoff: sequencing for MSA/DPA/order-form and evidence windows

Anna / Evelyn — attaching a preliminary MSA redline that scope-limits the pilot (confidential data segregation clause + limited liability for pilot usage). Also attached is an evidence inventory that maps each DPA artifact to the owner at Redwood.

Highlights:
- We can issue the MSA redline today and request a 3-business-day comment turnaround from ClearStream legal to stay on the 10/01 pilot cadence.
- For SOC2: if ClearStream accepts a SOC2-in-progress + a signed remediation plan we’ll mark the DPA as conditional (this must be explicit in the DPA).
- Proposed gating language for the order form: order form execution is conditioned on DPA signature or an agreed conditional DPA acceptance where both parties sign an evidence remediation plan.

Please review; Evelyn I left a few placeholders that standardize the pilot acceptance criteria (we should confirm with engineering).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
